step: STEP 5 - corner-aware retrain (re-opened because LOOP-9 was measured on the invalid GT)
decision_rule: If the retrained model's recall@D=5 is below pm_v10's 83.7% (TP@D=5 < 901), then steps 4 and 5 are recorded DEAD-BY-EVIDENCE and are NOT attempted.
reason: The premise for re-opening was that LOOP-9's corner-regression verdict (per-corner D=5 recall 59% -> quad 15%) was measured on 2026-10-14 against Compare-V1, i.e. on a less precise target than the true GT (P3: best orthogonal rectangle to the GT corners within p50 0.50 / max 1.32 px). That premise stands. But a corner-aware objective is a REFINEMENT of a detector that must first find the box, and the re-baselined OBB detector on the true GT finds only 234 TP at D=5 versus pm_v10's 901. Refining the corners of 234 detections cannot reach 901; the detection stage has to work first.

reference.p3_gt_precision: best strictly-orthogonal rectangle to the GT corners: minimax residual p50 0.50 / p90 0.80 / max 1.32 px
reference.loop9_original: D=5 TP 151 vs pm_v5's 502, per-corner D=5 recall 59% -> quad 15% (measured 2026-10-14, pre-GT-repointing)

caveat: Not attempted under the mechanical rule; this is NOT evidence that a corner-aware loss cannot work. It is evidence that it cannot be the next lever while the underlying detector recall is 234/901. The blocker is compute: ~56k labelled real images exist, but no GPU is available and one 90-minute CPU run buys ~300-2000 training images.
